{{Short description|Model in classical and quantum mechanics}}
'''Ruijsenaars–Schneider models''' (short '''RS models''') are [[Theory of relativity|relativistic]] generalizations of [[Calogero–Moser–Sutherland model|Calogero–Moser–Sutherland models]] (short CMS models), which are closely connected with [[Relativistic field theory|relativistic field theories]] like the [[Sine-Gordon equation|Sine-Gordon model]]. RS models are named after Simon N. M.  Ruijsenaars and Harald Schneider. Both of them introduced the [[Classical physics|classical]] models in 1986 and Ruijsenaars introduced the [[quantum]] models in 1987.<ref>Hallnäs 2023, p. 2</ref>

== Description ==
For <math>N</math> particles on the real line <math>\mathbb{R}</math>, the Hamiltonian of the RS model is given by:<ref>Ruijsenaars 1987, Equation (1.1)</ref>

: <math>H
=mc^2\sum_{i=1}^N\cosh\left(\frac{p_i}{mc}\right)\prod_{\stackrel{1\leq j\leq N}{j\neq i}}f(x_i-x_j).</math>

Different [[Potential energy|potentials]] lead to different RS models, which the four types most often considered being:

* Type I/rational:
*: <math>f(x)^2
=1+\left(\frac{g}{mcx}\right)^2.</math>
* Type II/hyperbolic:
*: <math>f(x)^2
=1+\frac{\sin\left(\frac{ag}{mc}\right)^2}{\sinh(ax)^2}.</math>
* Type III/trigonometric:
*: <math>f(x)^2
=1+\frac{\sinh\left(\frac{ag}{mc}\right)^2}{\sin(ax)^2}.</math>
* Type IV/elliptic:<ref>Ruijsenaars 1987, Equation (1.4)</ref>
*: <math>f(x)^2
=a+b\weierp(x;\omega_1,\omega_2).</math>
